title: Boosting the cardiorespiratory system

draft.title: Boosting the cardiorespiratory system
card: Altitude training
Athletes train at high places where the air has less oxygen. The body makes more red blood cells, so it can carry more oxygen. This is legal.
EPO
Erythropoietin (EPO) is a hormone that makes the body produce more red blood cells. It is banned. It can thicken the blood and raise the risk of clots, stroke and heart attack.
Blood doping
This means adding red blood cells to the body, using an athlete's own blood or a donor's. It is banned. Risks include infection, clots and strain on the heart.
Beta blockers
These drugs slow the heart rate and steady the hands. They help in sports such as archery and shooting, and are banned in those sports. They can cause tiredness and a very low heart rate.
draft.remember: Altitude training is legal. EPO, blood doping and beta blockers are banned and carry risks.

a.q: Which method of boosting the cardiorespiratory system is allowed in sport?
opts: Training at altitude
Using EPO
Blood doping
Using beta blockers
a.why: Altitude training is legal because the body makes extra red blood cells naturally. EPO and blood doping also raise red blood cells, but they are banned. Beta blockers are banned too.
a.clue: One method relies on the body's natural response to thin air.

b.q: Tom, a rower in Geelong, wants more red blood cells to carry oxygen. Which choice raises red blood cells and is legal?
opts: Camping at a high-altitude training centre
Injecting EPO before the regional titles
Receiving a transfusion of his own stored blood
Taking beta blockers to slow his heart rate
b.why: Altitude training makes the body produce more red blood cells naturally and is legal. A transfusion of his own blood is still blood doping, so it is banned even though the blood is his. Beta blockers do not raise red blood cells.
b.clue: Using your own blood is still blood doping.

b.best: Camping at a high-altitude training centre

problems.detail: The remember line says beta blockers are banned with no limit. The card says they are banned only in sports such as archery and shooting. Under WADA rules, beta blockers are allowed in most sports.

The question asks which method is 'allowed in sport' in general. Beta blockers are allowed in most sports, including running and rowing, so 'Using beta blockers' can be defended as right. Ask about one named sport such as archery, or ask which method raises red blood cells and is legal.
